title: Does recent painting history reduce redraws?

clips.label: Latest painting + RIFE
clips.note: Fresh noise · latest image latent · RIFE finishing
clips.details:
The same generated paintings as the corresponding raw clip, finished with our established RIFE 4.25 scale 1 interpolation. No new diffusion and no change to painting timestamps. Compare the matching raw clips to separate diffusion changes from interpolation artifacts.

The previous experiment repeatedly returned to one fixed source. This experiment instead encodes the newest completed painting and uses it to initialize the next repaint. This control adds a fresh independent noise pattern each time.

The city prompt stays unchanged; there is no spatial motion. Krea Turbo, CFG 1, starting noise 0.6, three Euler intervals. All four versions start with the same painting and identical first repaint.

clips.label: Recent history + RIFE
clips.note: Fresh noise · recent image latents 70/20/10 · RIFE finishing
clips.details:
The same generated paintings as the corresponding raw clip, finished with our established RIFE 4.25 scale 1 interpolation. No new diffusion and no change to painting timestamps. Compare the matching raw clips to separate diffusion changes from interpolation artifacts.

Instead of using only the newest painting's encoded image latent, mix the most recent three: 70% newest, 20% previous and 10% older. Early paints normalize the available weights. The latest painting always contributes; this is recurrent feedback, not a fixed opening.

These are clean image latents produced by VAE encoding, not random noise. The mix initializes sampling; no old pixels are pasted over the result. Fresh independent noise is the same sequence used in the control.

The scene is stationary so the history shares the same coordinate system. Any benefit here remains untested under warping or changing prompts. Same sigma 0.6, CFG 1, three Euler intervals, four paintings/s and 24 fps.

clips.label: Raw · Fresh noise · latest painting
clips.note: Control · each painting feeds the next · no history mix
clips.details:
The previous experiment repeatedly returned to one fixed source. This experiment instead encodes the newest completed painting and uses it to initialize the next repaint. This control adds a fresh independent noise pattern each time.

The city prompt stays unchanged; there is no spatial motion. Krea Turbo, CFG 1, starting noise 0.6, three Euler intervals. All four versions start with the same painting and identical first repaint.

Fifteen new paintings plus the opening, four paintings per second over four seconds at 24 fps. These are raw diagnostic videos: each painting is held for six frames. No RIFE. Shift+arrow steps through paintings.

clips.label: Raw · Gentle noise · latest painting
clips.note: Same feedback · noise pattern changes gradually
clips.details:
The newest completed painting still feeds the next repaint. Only the random pattern changes: adjacent noise correlation is0.995, with a fresh innovation coefficient of about 0.10. This is much gentler pattern evolution than the earlier 0.85 correlated-noise test.

Starting noise strength stays 0.6. A slowly changing random pattern does not necessarily preserve the artwork, because the image input is changing too. Compare with Fresh noise to assess this factor alone.

Same stationary city, prompt, CFG 1, three Euler intervals, four paintings/s and 24 fps raw holds. No RIFE.

clips.label: Raw · Fresh noise · recent history
clips.details:
Instead of using only the newest painting's encoded image latent, mix the most recent three: 70% newest, 20% previous and 10% older. Early paints normalize the available weights. The latest painting always contributes; this is recurrent feedback, not a fixed opening.

These are clean image latents produced by VAE encoding, not random noise. The mix initializes sampling; no old pixels are pasted over the result. Fresh independent noise is the same sequence used in the control.

The scene is stationary so the history shares the same coordinate system. Any benefit here remains untested under warping or changing prompts. Same sigma 0.6, CFG 1, three Euler intervals, four paintings/s and 24 fps raw holds. No RIFE.

clips.label: Raw · Gentle noise · recent history
clips.note: Recent image-latent mix + slowly changing noise
clips.details:
Combines the recent three image-latent weights 70/20/10 with noise correlation 0.995. Compare with Gentle noise/latest painting to isolate the history effect, or Fresh noise/recent history to isolate the noise-pattern effect.

History might damp sudden redesign, but could also soften details or reinforce accumulated artifacts. Preventing the earlier mosaic appearance is a hypothesis, not a guaranteed property of averaging.

Same fixed city prompt, no motion, sigma 0.6, CFG 1, three Euler intervals. Fifteen recurrent repaints plus the opening; four paintings/s over four seconds at 24 fps. Raw held paintings without RIFE.
